scope: Two native-720p topology-lock compositor attempts for the complete 27.5-second flower replacement
summary: Both candidates preserved the source flowers and background but were rejected by high-resolution human review because the transported canonical hand sprites became small, detached, duplicated, or implausibly scaled.
evidence: V1 processed 660 frames in 108.24 seconds at 6.10 FPS; V2 processed them in 58.91 seconds at 11.20 FPS.
Both candidates preserved every protected flower pixel before encoding and retained source flower motion on 98.01% of frame transitions.
The V1 review exposed giant late flower/base artifacts plus floating hands; the V2 review still exposed tiny detached hands and neon late material artifacts.
lessons: A canonical 2-D sprite cannot be transported through large occlusion and viewpoint changes using a single similarity transform.
Automatic preservation metrics cannot override high-resolution topology review.
limitations: No physical depth, force, telemetry, or execution claim is made.
next_actions: Replace sprite transport with official Wan2.2-Animate-14B local window generation and route only reviewed windows.
